title: Token-rush stabilizer for multi-tenant weighted routing
creator: Priya Desai
description: Multiple enterprise customers (hosted + dedicated private nodes) reported sudden TTFT and tokens/sec collapses during short bursts of concurrent requests. Root cause appears correlated with our weighted routing policy that momentarily pushes a high volume of small, high-priority requests to the same backend set, triggering aggressive KV prefetch + speculative kernel selection which overwhelms kernel queues and causes GPU serialization and token throughput collapse. This ticket coordinates an urgent, minimally invasive stabilizer that prevents token-rush cascades while we validate a longer-term routing and kernel-selection redesign.
reproduction_steps: Stage a multi-tenant routing scenario: 100 tenants, weighted routing where 5 tenants have 3x weight each
Generate mixed-length prompt fanout: 700 short requests (context ~64 tokens) and 300 long requests (context ~2048 tokens) across the weighted tenants
Run sustained burst for 30s and observe scheduling, per-kernel queue depth and KV prefetch logs
Measure TTFT distribution, tokens/sec per worker, and GPU SM utilization; compare with a baseline run without weighted skew
observed_metrics: TTFT p95 increased from 120ms -> 950ms during bursts
tokens/sec per-GPU dropped by 60% for 10-30s windows
kernel queue depth spiked 4x; several kernels logged 'misselected-opt' warnings
KV prefetch IO multiplied by 3x causing CPU worker stalls and backpressure on multiplex queues
mitigation_applied: Deployed router-level token-rush circuit: thresholds on in-flight token-rate per-tenant to convert excess requests into queued/batched window
Temporarily disabled aggressive KV prefetch heuristics for affected model families to reduce CPU stalls
Added conservative kernel fallback: if kernel queue depth > 80% use baseline kernel with predictable latency
Instrumented extra tracing (router span + kernel selection tags) and added dashboards for quick triage
decision_notes: Short-term mitigations must be non-disruptive to SLA customers: we chose throttling at router-level rather than broad global rate limits
We will not change model variants or quantization in this hotfix to avoid quality regressions for customers
Permanent solution will likely combine adaptive routing heuristics and improved kernel selection gating; this ticket focuses on emergency containment + observability
